moduleTitle: Saving data to a system of record
learningObjectives: Configure a savable Data Page with the correct data save options to write data back to a system of record.
Trigger the save plan using a Save Data Page Automation Step and configure explicit or implicit Data Page references.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Savable Data Pages — Purpose and Configuration

elements.text: A savable page is like a draft form with a submission operation: edits and persistence are distinct. The save implementation determines how failures and transaction boundaries are handled; this analogy does not promise universal rollback across external systems.

elements.description: Pushes data FROM a Data Page TO a System of Record (SOR). Works for both Pega Platform's internal database and external SORs. Edit mode must be set to 'Savable'. A data save plan specifies how and where data is saved.

Flow and Flow Action invocation manage the Pega transaction automatically. An Activity invocation can choose its transaction boundary; custom Activity persistence must handle consistency and errors. Do not assume every remote API participates in an atomic rollback.

elements.term: When Conditions in the data save plan
elements.description: Configure When Conditions on each save target to commit to multiple data tables simultaneously. If a When Condition is true → the data commit runs. If all When Conditions are false → the Otherwise Condition runs.

Database save persists a Page-structure record to a configured database row. A Data Transform can prepare or map data when needed; it is not universally mandatory. The database operation has transactional integrity.

elements.term: Save options: Database update and Database delete
items: Database update: modifies an existing record in the internal SOR within the same transaction scope
Database delete: removes a record from the internal SOR

elements.description: Saves data to an external SOR using REST-based integration. REST ONLY — not SOAP. Use when the external system exposes a REST API.

elements.term: Save options: Robotic Automation and Robotic Desktop Automation
elements.description: RPA-based save options for external systems:
items: Robotic Automation: unattended RPA to write to an external system
Robotic Desktop Automation: desktop-driven RDA for UI-based external systems that have no API

elements.description: Activity supports custom persistence, including supported integrations such as SOAP. The implementation is responsible for transactionality and error handling; prefer dedicated options where sufficient.

elements.term: Update vs. Create — key and source
elements.description: Two savable Data Page operations driven by whether a key exists:
items: UPDATE — key IS PRESENT → use Lookup as source
CREATE — key NOT PRESENT → use Data Transform as source (one savable Data Page can support both)

elements.term: Auto-populated property + savable Data Page: Copy
elements.description: The current source recommends Copy data from a Data Page for this pattern. Refer can accidentally overwrite unsaved edits before the save is triggered. Use the associated-property save configuration to persist the edited property.
Provides a simple way to update data object information without complex configuration. Supports additional validation and pre/post-processing of data.

elements.term: 3 ways to trigger the save plan
elements.description: ① Add a Save Data Page Automation Step in a flow (AFTER an Assignment). ② Add post-processing for a Flow Action. ③ Call Save-DataPage in an Activity. When triggered from a flow or Flow Action, Pega manages transaction handling automatically.

For the lesson’s user-entered-data flow, place saving after the Assignment that collects the values. This is a sequencing recommendation for that flow, not a ban on other valid save invocation points.

elements.term: Multiple SOR commits in one flow
elements.description: The source recommends multiple Save Data Page Steps for multiple data sources. Do not generalize this into a ban on multiple conditional save options within one page’s save plan.

elements.term: Explicit vs. Implicit Data Page reference
elements.description: Two ways to reference a Data Page:
items: EXPLICIT — enter the Data Page Name directly; any parameters can be specified
IMPLICIT — Use associated property selects an auto-populated page/page-list property; parameters come from its property Rule.

examPitfalls.title: Savable Data Pages work for BOTH Pega Platform and external SORs
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask which save target requires a Savable Data Page. Candidates answer 'external systems only,' not realizing a Savable Data Page also writes to the internal Pega Platform database via the Database save option.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The save option targets the internal or external system of record; verify its supported integration and failure behavior.

examPitfalls.title: Connector data save option uses REST ONLY — not SOAP
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A scenario describes a SOAP web service and asks which save option to use. Candidates select 'Connector' because the target is external. Connector is REST-only — SOAP requires a different approach.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The Connector save option works with REST-based integrations ONLY. SOAP or other protocols require a different approach (e.g., Activity).

examPitfalls.title: Database save: Page structure, mapping when needed
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Do not confuse mapping to the target Data Model with explicitly mapping every clipboard property to a column.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Database save supports Page structure; a Data Transform can prepare or map values when needed.

examPitfalls.title: Savable autopopulation: Copy protects pending edits
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The old advice to always Refer reverses the current source caution: a reference may overwrite unsaved edits.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use Copy data from a Data Page for the described savable autopopulation pattern and configure saving through the associated property.

examPitfalls.title: Update = Lookup (key present); Create = Data Transform (key absent)
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question describes a savable Data Page handling both new and existing records. Candidates use Data Transform for both paths. Lookup (not Data Transform) handles the update path when the record key is already present.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Key present → Lookup (update existing). Key absent → Data Transform (create new). One savable Data Page supports both via conditional sourcing.

examPitfalls.title: Save Data Page Step goes AFTER an Assignment — not before
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask where in the Case Life Cycle to place the Save Data Page Step. Candidates place it before the Assignment. The Save Data Page Step must be placed AFTER the Assignment that collects the data — placing it before means no user data has been entered yet.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Save after the Assignment that supplies the values in this user-entry workflow.

examPitfalls.title: Multiple save Steps: the documented multi-source pattern
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The source recommends multiple Steps for multiple sources. A page can nevertheless have multiple conditional save options.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use the documented multiple-Step pattern and review each page’s save options; do not infer a universal one-target restriction.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The team will use a Data Page save plan to write HR seat assignments to a system of record. Which edit mode enables that plan?

options.text: Savable — enables a save plan to push Data Page contents to a system of record
Editable — allows the application to modify the Data Page contents in memory
Read-Only — streams data to the external system automatically
Requestor — persists data across all of the user's Cases

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish source loading, property editing, save-plan configuration and invocation.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Savable enables the requested save plan.

optionExplanations.A: Savable enables the requested save plan.
optionExplanations.B: Editable alone changes memory rather than enabling that plan.
optionExplanations.C: Read-Only does not automatically stream writes.
optionExplanations.D: Requestor controls visibility, not persistence mode.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which dedicated Connector save option directly persists through a supported external REST API?

options.text: Connector — saves to external SOR via REST-based integration
Database save — saves a single page to a database row
Robotic Automation — unattended RPA for external system writes
Activity — custom persistence logic via an Activity Rule

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish source loading, property editing, save-plan configuration and invocation.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Connector is the dedicated REST save option.

optionExplanations.A: Connector is the dedicated REST save option.
optionExplanations.B: Database save does not directly invoke the REST endpoint.
optionExplanations.C: Robotic Automation is not this dedicated connector option.
optionExplanations.D: Custom Activity logic is not the dedicated option requested.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the lesson’s conditional create/update example, when is Lookup selected as the source?

options.text: When a key is present — the record exists and needs to be updated
When no key is present — creating a new record for the first time
When the Data Page uses list structure instead of page structure
When the SOR is Pega Platform's internal database

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish source loading, property editing, save-plan configuration and invocation.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The example loads an existing keyed record with Lookup.

optionExplanations.A: The example loads an existing keyed record with Lookup.
optionExplanations.B: The new-record branch uses initialization logic.
optionExplanations.C: List structure alone does not identify the example’s update branch.
optionExplanations.D: An internal database alone does not determine whether a record exists.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO methods can trigger the save plan for a savable Data Page?

options.text: Add a Save Data Page Automation Step in a flow Rule
Add post-processing for a Flow Action Rule
Configure a Stage validation in the Case Life Cycle
Set the Data Page scope to Thread

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish source loading, property editing, save-plan configuration and invocation.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The flow automation invokes the plan. Flow Action post-processing can invoke it.

optionExplanations.A: The flow automation invokes the plan.
optionExplanations.B: Flow Action post-processing can invoke it.
optionExplanations.C: Stage validation alone is not a save invocation.
optionExplanations.D: Changing scope does not execute persistence.

practiceQuiz.scenario: For the savable Data Page autopopulation pattern in the current source, which configuration protects pending property edits against unintended refresh before saving?

options.text: Refer to a Data Page — always use a reference for savable autopopulation
Copy data from a Data Page — use the recommended copy pattern and save the associated property
Either Refer or Copy — both work the same for savable Data Pages
Copy data — required specifically when using the Database save option

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish source loading, property editing, save-plan configuration and invocation.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Copy is recommended for this savable autopopulation pattern.

optionExplanations.A: Always referring reverses the source’s caution about pending edits.
optionExplanations.B: Copy is recommended for this savable autopopulation pattern.
optionExplanations.C: The two patterns have different refresh and edit behavior.
optionExplanations.D: The database option does not establish this proposed exclusive requirement.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A user Assignment collects supplier registration details. Where should its Save Data Page Step be placed to persist those entered values?

options.text: After the Assignment — saves data after the user has entered or updated information
Before the Assignment — pre-populates the SOR before the user sees the form
At the start of the flow — saves data when the Case is created
At the end of the flow only — saves when the Case resolves

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish source loading, property editing, save-plan configuration and invocation.
practiceQuiz.rationale: After collection, the entered values are available to save.

optionExplanations.A: After collection, the entered values are available to save.
optionExplanations.B: Before entry does not persist those newly entered values.
optionExplanations.C: Case creation occurs before the requested Assignment values exist.
optionExplanations.D: Saving does not have to wait until resolution.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which flow pattern does the source recommend for committing data to two different external sources?

options.text: Add two separate Save Data Page Automation Steps — one per external API
Configure a single Save Data Page Step with both APIs listed as targets
Use Aggregate sources in the save plan to write to both APIs simultaneously
Use a When Condition in the save plan to alternate between the two APIs

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish source loading, property editing, save-plan configuration and invocation.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Separate save Steps are the recommended flow pattern.

optionExplanations.A: Separate save Steps are the recommended flow pattern.
optionExplanations.B: The automation field is not a list of API targets.
optionExplanations.C: Aggregate sources is a loading option rather than this flow save pattern.
optionExplanations.D: Alternating targets does not ensure both receive updates.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Save Data Page Automation Step references a Data Page implicitly. What must the SA configure?

options.text: 'Use associated property' — select an autopopulated property; its associated Data Page is referenced automatically
The Data Page Name field — enter the Data Page name directly
'Copy data from Data Page' — specify the source Data Page
The Audit Note field — specify the SOR to write to

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish source loading, property editing, save-plan configuration and invocation.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The associated property supplies its page and parameters.

optionExplanations.A: The associated property supplies its page and parameters.
optionExplanations.B: Naming the page directly is explicit configuration.
optionExplanations.C: Copy is an autopopulation setting, not the implicit-reference selector.
optionExplanations.D: An Audit Note records save context rather than selecting a target.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which database save option removes a record from the internal SOR as part of a transactional operation?

options.text: Database delete
Database update
Database save
Connector

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish source loading, property editing, save-plan configuration and invocation.

optionExplanations.B: Update modifies a record instead of removing it.
optionExplanations.C: Save persists record data rather than selecting deletion.
optionExplanations.D: Connector is not the named internal database deletion option.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Pega Platform automatically manages transaction handling when the save plan is triggered from which source?

options.text: From a flow Rule or Flow Action — Pega manages transaction handling automatically
From an Activity Rule only — Activities provide built-in transaction management
All three trigger methods manage transactions identically
Transaction management must always be configured manually by the SA

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish source loading, property editing, save-plan configuration and invocation.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The source identifies automatic handling for these invocation points.

optionExplanations.A: The source identifies automatic handling for these invocation points.
optionExplanations.B: An Activity chooses its transaction scope; it is not the only automatic path.
optionExplanations.C: Activity boundary choices mean the methods are not identical.
optionExplanations.D: Flow-managed handling disproves the claim that everything is manual.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which single-page conditional sourcing approach matches the lesson’s existing-record versus new-record example?

options.text: Conditional: Lookup when key exists (update); Data Transform when key absent (create)
Always use Data Transform — it handles both create and update
Always use Lookup — it creates new records when none exist
Create two separate savable Data Pages — one for create, one for update

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish source loading, property editing, save-plan configuration and invocation.
practiceQuiz.rationale: This matches the conditional sourcing example on one page.

optionExplanations.A: This matches the conditional sourcing example on one page.
optionExplanations.B: An initialization transform is not the example’s existing-record lookup.
optionExplanations.C: Lookup is not the example’s blank new-record initialization.
optionExplanations.D: Separate pages do not answer the requested single-page approach.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is designing a Savable Data Page to write customer address updates back to an external CRM system and needs to verify the available save options and how the save is triggered. Which TWO statements correctly describe how Savable Data Pages are configured to write data?

options.text: Savable Data Pages can write to both Pega Platform's internal database and external SORs
The Connector save option supports both REST and SOAP integrations
When Conditions in the data save plan allow committing to multiple data tables
The save plan can only be triggered by a Save Data Page Automation Step

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish source loading, property editing, save-plan configuration and invocation.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The plan supports internal and external systems of record. Conditions determine which configured save operations run.

optionExplanations.A: The plan supports internal and external systems of record.
optionExplanations.B: The dedicated Connector save option is REST-only in this context.
optionExplanations.C: Conditions determine which configured save operations run.
optionExplanations.D: Post-processing and Activity invocation are also documented.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A developer is configuring a Savable Data Page to write updated customer contact information back to an external CRM system. Which TWO statements correctly describe how Savable Data Pages work?

options.text: A Savable Data Page is configured with data save options that define how and where the data is written back to the system of record
A Save Data Page Automation Step in the Case workflow explicitly triggers the save plan to commit the changes to the external system
A Savable Data Page automatically writes all changes to the source system whenever any property on the page is modified
The Save Data Page Automation Step must always be placed in the first Step of the first Stage to function correctly

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish source loading, property editing, save-plan configuration and invocation.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Save options define the persistence implementation. The automation triggers the configured plan at its workflow point.

optionExplanations.A: Save options define the persistence implementation.
optionExplanations.B: The automation triggers the configured plan at its workflow point.
optionExplanations.C: Editing a value alone does not invoke the save plan.
optionExplanations.D: The automation is not universally restricted to the first Step.

quickRecap.value: Pushes data FROM Data Page TO SOR (Pega or external). Edit mode = Savable. Requires a data save plan.
Database save/update/delete, Connector (REST), Robotic Automation, Robotic desktop Automation, Activity.
Page structure. Map or prepare data when needed; database operation is transactional.
① Save Data Page Automation Step in flow (after Assignment). ② Flow Action post-processing. ③ Save-DataPage Activity method.
Key present → Lookup (update existing). Key absent → Data Transform (create new).
Current source recommends Copy for savable autopopulation to avoid accidental overwrites before saving.
Multiple Steps are the recommended multi-source flow pattern; a plan can contain conditional save options.
Explicit = Data Page Name field. Implicit = 'Use associated property' (resolves automatically).
